gt.en: Children go from house to house and say, “Trick or treat!” Neighbours give them candy.
gt.zh: 孩子們挨家挨戶地說：「不給糖就搗蛋！」鄰居就給他們糖果。

gt.en: Homes are covered in spider webs, bats, and paper skeletons.
gt.zh: 家家戶戶都掛滿了蜘蛛網、蝙蝠和紙做的骷髏。

tz: 10 月 31 日是萬聖節。這是一個有趣又有點可怕的夜晚，受到許多國家的孩子喜愛。
人們會穿上萬聖節服裝，打扮成鬼、女巫、超級英雄，甚至是貓！
孩子們挨家挨戶地說：「不給糖就搗蛋！」鄰居們就會給他們糖果。
家人們會一起刻南瓜。他們在南瓜上刻出一張嚇人的臉，再在裡面放一盞燈。這叫做南瓜燈。
家家戶戶掛滿了蜘蛛網、蝙蝠和紙做的骷髏。一切看起來都有點可怕——但全都只是為了好玩。
萬聖節是一個充滿遊戲、糖果和想像力的夜晚。你想穿什麼樣的服裝呢？

b.title: The Night of Costumes
text: Every 31 October, streets fill with tiny ghosts and witches as families celebrate Halloween, one of the world's most playful holidays.

Its roots are ancient. More than two thousand years ago, the Celtic people of Ireland held a festival called Samhain. They believed that on this night the world of the living and the world of the dead came close, so they lit fires and wore disguises to confuse wandering spirits.
Over the centuries the festival mixed with Christian traditions and travelled to America, where it grew into the modern Halloween of costumes, candy, and carved pumpkins.

The famous jack-o'-lantern comes from an old Irish tale about a man named Jack, who could enter neither heaven nor hell and wandered the dark with a lantern made from a turnip. In America, people used pumpkins instead.
Today Halloween is big business, with huge sums spent on sweets and costumes. It has also spread far beyond the West, appearing in shops and parties across Asia.
Beneath the fun lies something old and very human: a playful way to face the dark, and to laugh at the things that frighten us.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The jack-o'-lantern comes from an old Irish tale about a man named Jack.
A playful holiday today, Halloween grew from an ancient festival of the dead.
Today Halloween is big business, with huge spending on sweets and costumes.
Samhain was a Celtic festival in Ireland marking the end of the harvest.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文。

q.q: What was Samhain?
opts: A Celtic festival held in Ireland
An American candy company
A Roman god of the dead
An Irish story about a man named Jack
q.why: 原文：“More than two thousand years ago, the Celtic people of Ireland held a festival called Samhain.”

q.q: Where does the jack-o'-lantern come from?
opts: An American pumpkin farm in the 1800s
A Celtic god who carried a lantern
A popular modern horror film
An old Irish tale about a man named Jack
q.why: 原文：“The famous jack-o'-lantern comes from an old Irish tale about a man named Jack, who could enter neither heaven nor hell and wandered the dark with a lantern made …”

q.q: In paragraph 2, a “disguise” is ___.
opts: a special kind of Halloween candy
a scary decoration hung on a door
clothes or looks that hide who you are
a large fire lit to keep people warm
q.why: disguise = 偽裝。

q.q: What does “a playful way to face the dark” suggest about Halloween?
opts: It makes people more afraid of the dark than before
It lets people laugh at, and cope with, their fears
It is really only about collecting free candy
It should be celebrated only after it gets dark
q.why: 線索：“Beneath the fun lies something old and very human: a playful way to face the dark, and to laugh at the things that frighten us.”

q.q: Someone says: “Halloween is just an American shopping holiday.” Which fact from the text best challenges this?
opts: People now spend a lot of money on sweets
Children knock on doors and say “Trick or treat!”
It grew from Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival
Homes are decorated with bats and spider webs
q.why: 萬聖節源自愛爾蘭古老的薩溫節，不只是美國購物節。

tr.en: Every 31 October, streets fill with tiny ghosts and witches as families celebrate Halloween, one of the world's most playful holidays.
tr.zh: 每年十月三十一日，街上到處都是小小的鬼和女巫，因為家家戶戶都在慶祝萬聖節——全世界最愛玩的節日之一。

tr.en: More than two thousand years ago, the Celtic people of Ireland held a festival called Samhain.
tr.zh: 兩千多年前，愛爾蘭的凱爾特人會舉行一個叫做薩溫節的節慶。

tr.en: Today Halloween is big business, with huge sums spent on sweets and costumes.
tr.zh: 今天，萬聖節是一門大生意，人們在糖果和服裝上花了大筆的錢。

tz: 每年 10 月 31 日，街上擠滿了小鬼和小女巫，家家戶戶都在慶祝萬聖節——世界上最好玩的節日之一。
它的根源非常古老。兩千多年前，愛爾蘭的凱爾特人會舉辦一個叫做「薩溫節」的節慶。他們相信在這一晚，活人的世界和亡者的世界會靠得很近，所以會點起火堆、穿上偽裝，來迷惑四處遊蕩的靈魂。
經過幾個世紀，這個節慶和基督教的傳統融合，再傳到美國，在那裡發展成現代這個有服裝、糖果和雕刻南瓜的萬聖節。
著名的南瓜燈來自一個古老的愛爾蘭故事：一個名叫傑克的人，既上不了天堂、也下不了地獄，只能提著一盞用蕪菁做的燈籠在黑暗中遊蕩。到了美國，人們改用南瓜來做。
今天，萬聖節是一門大生意，人們在糖果和服裝上花了巨額的錢。它也已經傳到西方以外很遠的地方，出現在亞洲各地的商店和派對裡。
在這些樂趣底下，藏著某種古老而非常人性的東西：一種用好玩的方式面對黑暗、笑看那些讓我們害怕的事物的方法。

c.title: Laughing at the Dark
text: Each 31 October much of the world gives itself over to a strange and cheerful ritual: dressing up as the very things it fears. Halloween, beneath its plastic fangs and sugar, is older and stranger than it looks.

Its distant ancestor is Samhain, the Celtic festival that marked the year's turn toward winter. On that night, it was believed, the border between the living and the dead grew thin; fires were lit and disguises worn, less in celebration than in wary respect for whatever might be abroad.

What is striking is how the meaning has inverted. A festival once shaped by a genuine fear of the dead has become a carnival in which death is domesticated — worn as a costume, handed out as candy, propped up as a plastic skeleton on a suburban lawn. The terror has been tamed into play.

Some lament this as commercial excess, and the sums spent each year are indeed extraordinary. Yet there may be something quietly healthy in it. Every culture needs a way to look at mortality without flinching, and a society that can laugh at skeletons is, perhaps, a little less afraid of the real thing.
That is Halloween's sly achievement: it takes the oldest of human fears and, for one night, turns it into a doorbell, a costume, and a child's delighted shriek.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Halloween today is essentially the same as the ancient festival of Samhain.
Halloween should return to its serious religious and spiritual roots.
Halloween has become harmful because it is far too commercial now.
Halloween turns an ancient fear of death into a playful celebration.
q.why: 主軸：把古老的死亡恐懼轉化成趣味。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “death is domesticated” means death is ___.
opts: made much more frightening
completely forgotten about
tamed and made unthreatening
treated as a holy subject
q.why: domesticate = 馴化。

q.q: What does the writer mean by “the meaning has inverted”?
opts: A festival of real fear has become a playful carnival
People now fear death more than they did in the past
The festival moved from Ireland across to America
Children now lead the festival instead of adults
q.why: 線索：“A festival once shaped by a genuine fear of the dead has become a carnival in which death is domesticated — worn as a costume, handed out as candy, propped up as a …”

q.q: How does the writer treat the commercial side of Halloween?
opts: Completely approves of all the spending
Admits the excess, yet finds something healthy
Completely rejects it as harmful waste
Praises the spending as the true heart of it
q.why: 第四段。

q.q: What is the function of the word “Yet” in paragraph 4?
opts: To add another complaint about the spending
To introduce a quotation from a historian
To turn from complaint to a positive reframing
To bring the essay to its conclusion
q.why: Yet 為轉折。

q.q: Which activity best shows the writer's idea of facing fears through play?
opts: Children dressing as monsters and laughing together
Watching a frightening news report all alone
Children telling each other that monsters really exist
Telling young children that monsters are real
q.why: 用遊戲、扮裝笑看可怕的東西，正是作者的觀點。

tz: 每年 10 月 31 日，世界上很多地方都會沉浸在一個奇怪又歡樂的儀式裡：把自己打扮成自己害怕的東西。在塑膠尖牙和糖果底下，萬聖節比它看起來的更古老、也更奇特。
它遙遠的祖先是薩溫節，一個標誌著一年轉入冬天的凱爾特節慶。人們相信，在那一晚，活人與亡者之間的界線會變得很薄；人們點起火堆、穿上偽裝，與其說是慶祝，不如說是對任何可能在外遊蕩的東西保持警惕的敬意。
引人注目的是，它的意義已經翻轉了。一個曾經由對亡者真實的恐懼所塑造的節慶，變成了一場「死亡被馴服」的嘉年華——死亡被當成服裝穿上身、被當成糖果發出去、被當成塑膠骷髏立在郊區的草坪上。恐懼被馴化成了遊戲。
有些人感嘆這是一種商業上的過度，而每年花掉的錢確實驚人。然而，這裡面或許有某種默默健康的東西。每一個文化都需要一種能不退縮地直視死亡的方法，而一個能笑看骷髏的社會，或許對真正的死亡也就少了一點害怕。
這就是萬聖節狡黠的成就：它把人類最古老的恐懼，在一個晚上之內，變成了一聲門鈴、一套服裝，以及一個孩子開心的尖叫。

discuss: Do people celebrate Halloween in Taiwan? How is it similar to or different from local festivals?
Halloween lets us “play” with scary things. Why do you think humans enjoy being a little scared?
Some say Halloween is too commercial. Do you agree? Can a holiday be both fun and meaningful?

topic: World Cities Day
zh: 世界城市日：未來的城市長什麼樣子？

a.title: Living Together in Cities
text: October 31 is Halloween, but it is also World Cities Day. The United Nations started this day in 2014.
More than half of all people in the world live in cities. Many more people will move to cities in the future.
Cities have good things. There are schools, hospitals, jobs and fun places to visit.
But big cities also have problems. There can be traffic jams, dirty air and expensive homes.
On World Cities Day, people think about how to make cities better: more parks, cleaner buses, and safe places to walk and ride bikes.
What would make your city a better place to live?

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Why more and more people live in cities
Problems like traffic jams in big cities
World Cities Day and how to make cities better
Why people should move out of cities to the country
q.why: 全文介紹世界城市日與改善城市。

q.q: Who started World Cities Day?
opts: A city in Taiwan
The United Nations
A group of mayors
The city of Shanghai
q.why: 原文：“The United Nations started this day in 2014.”

q.q: Which is a problem in big cities?
opts: Traffic jams
Too few schools
Too many parks
Not enough jobs
q.why: 原文：“There can be traffic jams, dirty air and expensive homes.”

q.q: In the text, “expensive” means ___.
opts: very crowded with people
very new and modern
far away from the centre
costing a lot of money
q.why: expensive = 昂貴的。

q.q: Why does the text end with a question?
opts: To test readers on the facts
Because the writer does not know the answer
To make readers think about their own city
To introduce another article
q.why: 線索：“On World Cities Day, people think about how to make cities better: more parks, cleaner buses, and safe places to walk and ride bikes.”

q.q: Your city wants to make life better for students. Which idea fits the text best?
opts: Build safe paths for walking and cycling to school
Build more roads that only cars are allowed to use
Remove the parks so that new shops can be built
Make bus tickets more expensive for everyone
q.why: 文章提到更多公園、乾淨公車、安全步行與騎車的地方。

gt.en: October 31 is Halloween, but it is also World Cities Day.
gt.zh: 十月三十一日是萬聖節，但它也是世界城市日。

gt.en: More than half of all people in the world live in cities.
gt.zh: 全世界超過一半的人住在城市裡。

gt.en: There are schools, hospitals, jobs and fun places to visit.
gt.zh: 城市裡有學校、醫院、工作機會，還有好玩的地方可以去。

gt.en: But big cities also have problems.
gt.zh: 但是大城市也有一些問題。

tz: 10 月 31 日是萬聖節，但它也是世界城市日。聯合國在 2014 年設立了這個日子。
全世界一半以上的人住在城市裡。將來還會有更多人搬到城市。
城市有很多好處，有學校、醫院、工作機會，還有好玩的地方可以去。
但大城市也有問題，可能會有塞車、髒空氣和很貴的房子。
在世界城市日，人們會想想如何讓城市變得更好：更多公園、更乾淨的公車，以及可以安全走路和騎腳踏車的地方。
怎麼樣能讓你的城市變成一個更好住的地方呢？

b.title: A Planet of City Dwellers
text: October 31 is best known for Halloween, but since 2014 it has also been World Cities Day, set up by the United Nations to focus attention on how we live in urban areas.
The day grew out of the 2010 World Expo in Shanghai, whose slogan was 'Better City, Better Life'. The first official World Cities Day was held there.
The numbers explain why it matters. Today more than half of the world's population lives in cities, and the UN expects that share to reach about two-thirds by 2050.

Cities can be engines of opportunity, offering jobs, universities and hospitals. Yet rapid growth also brings overcrowding, pollution, rising rents and, in poorer countries, informal settlements without clean water.

Each year the UN picks a theme, from climate change to affordable housing. Planners around the world use the day to share ideas such as better public transport, green spaces and streets designed for people rather than cars.
Taiwan, where most people already live in cities, faces the same questions: how to keep growing while staying liveable.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The day argues that cities should stop growing and that people should move back to villages.
The day highlights urban growth and how cities can grow yet stay liveable.
The UN expects about two-thirds of people to live in cities by 2050.
Cities offer people jobs, universities, hospitals and cultural life.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文。

q.q: Where did World Cities Day grow out of?
opts: The 2010 World Expo in Shanghai
A UN meeting in New York in 2010
The 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing
A conference on cities held in Taipei
q.why: 原文：“The day grew out of the 2010 World Expo in Shanghai, whose slogan was 'Better City, Better Life'.”

q.q: What share of people does the UN expect to live in cities by 2050?
opts: About a half
About one-third
About two-thirds
Almost everyone
q.why: 第三段。半數是今天的情況。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “affordable” housing is housing that ___.
opts: is close to the city centre
is very large
is newly built
people can pay for
q.why: affordable = 負擔得起的。

q.q: Why does the writer mention Taiwan at the end?
opts: Taiwan was the country that started World Cities Day
Taiwan has already solved all of its city problems
The same city questions apply to readers' own home
Taiwan has very few large cities compared with others
q.why: 把議題拉回台灣。

q.q: A city has many new jobs, but rents have doubled and families are moving away. Which idea from the text best describes this problem?
opts: Cities never really offer many new jobs to people
Rapid growth can bring rising rents with opportunity
Building more parks always causes rents to rise
Only small towns, not cities, have rising rents
q.why: 第四段：成長帶來機會，也帶來房租上漲。

tr.en: The day grew out of the 2010 World Expo in Shanghai, whose slogan was 'Better City, Better Life'.
tr.zh: 這個節日源自 2010 年的上海世界博覽會，那次世博的標語是「城市，讓生活更美好」。

tr.en: Today more than half of the world's population lives in cities, and the UN expects that share to reach about two-thirds by 2050.
tr.zh: 今天，全世界超過一半的人口住在城市裡，而聯合國預估到 2050 年，這個比例會達到大約三分之二。

tr.en: Cities can be engines of opportunity, offering jobs, universities and hospitals.
tr.zh: 城市可以是機會的引擎，提供工作、大學和醫院。

tz: 10 月 31 日最有名的是萬聖節，但從 2014 年起，它也是世界城市日；聯合國設立這個日子，是為了讓人們關注我們在城市地區如何生活。
這個日子源自 2010 年的上海世界博覽會，那屆世博的口號是「城市，讓生活更美好」。第一屆正式的世界城市日也在那裡舉行。
數字說明了它為什麼重要。今天，全世界一半以上的人口住在城市，聯合國預估到 2050 年，這個比例會達到大約三分之二。
城市可以是機會的引擎，提供工作、大學和醫院。然而，快速的成長也帶來過度擁擠、污染、不斷上漲的房租；在比較貧窮的國家，還有沒有乾淨用水的非正式聚落。
聯合國每年都會挑選一個主題，從氣候變遷到可負擔的住宅都有。世界各地的規劃者利用這一天分享各種想法，例如更好的大眾運輸、綠地，以及為人、而不是為車設計的街道。
台灣大多數人已經住在城市裡，也面臨同樣的問題：如何持續成長，同時保持宜居。

c.title: The Century of the City
text: If the twentieth century was the age of the nation, the twenty-first may be remembered as the century of the city. World Cities Day, designated by the United Nations and first observed on October 31, 2014, exists to make that shift visible.
The arithmetic is striking. Over half of humanity is now urban, and UN projections suggest roughly two in three people will live in cities by 2050, with most of the growth in Asia and Africa.

Cities concentrate both promise and peril. Density makes it cheaper to deliver schools, clinics and transport, and it brings together the talent that drives innovation. The same density, unmanaged, produces congestion, polluted air, unaffordable housing and sprawling informal settlements.

Climate makes the stakes higher. Urban areas consume much of the world's energy, yet they are also where the most efficient solutions — compact housing, mass transit, walkable streets — are easiest to adopt.

Ultimately, the question World Cities Day poses is not whether people will move to cities, but what kind of cities they will find. The answer will be shaped less by grand plans than by countless local choices about who streets, parks and homes are really built for.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The key question is whether people will keep moving to cities at all.
The key question is what kind of cities we build, through local choices.
Grand national plans alone will decide the future shape of cities.
The twenty-first century belongs to nations rather than to cities.
q.why: 主旨：關鍵在於打造怎樣的城市。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “density” refers to ___.
opts: how tall the buildings in a city are
how old a city is compared with others
how much money people living in a city earn
how closely people or buildings are packed
q.why: density = 密度。

q.q: Why does the writer say cities “concentrate both promise and peril”?
opts: The closeness that makes services efficient also crowds
Cities simply have more banks and police than towns
Cities are dangerous places, but only at night
The same closeness makes cities both richer and always safer
q.why: 第三段。

q.q: What is the writer's tone?
opts: Completely optimistic about cities
Completely pessimistic about cities
Balanced, mixing hope with concern
Angry at the city planners involved
q.why: 審慎平衡。

q.q: How does the final paragraph reframe the issue?
opts: It repeats the population figures from the start
From 'will people move?' to 'what cities will they find?'
It argues that big cities should stop growing
From 'what cities will they find?' to 'will people move?'
q.why: 結尾轉換提問。

q.q: According to the writer, which decision would MOST shape what kind of city people find?
opts: A global report on population trends to the year 2050
A famous slogan first used at the 2010 World Expo
A council deciding if a street is for cars or for people
The date chosen each year for World Cities Day
q.why: 結尾：許多在地選擇（街道、公園、住宅為誰而建）決定城市樣貌。

tz: 如果說二十世紀是民族國家的時代，二十一世紀可能會被記為城市的世紀。由聯合國指定、在 2014 年 10 月 31 日首次舉行的世界城市日，就是為了讓這個轉變被看見而存在的。
算一算就令人驚訝。如今超過一半的人類住在城市裡，而聯合國預估，到了 2050 年，大約每三個人就有兩個會住在城市，其中大部分的成長發生在亞洲和非洲。
城市同時集中了希望與危險。人口密集讓提供學校、診所和交通變得比較便宜，也把推動創新的人才聚集在一起。但同樣的密度，如果沒有好好管理，就會產生交通壅塞、空氣污染、負擔不起的住宅，以及不斷蔓延的非正式聚落。
氣候讓風險變得更高。城市地區消耗了全世界大部分的能源，然而也正是在城市裡，最有效率的解決方法——緊湊的住宅、大眾運輸、適合步行的街道——最容易被採用。
說到底，世界城市日提出的問題，不是人們會不會搬到城市，而是他們會在那裡找到什麼樣的城市。答案與其說取決於宏大的計畫，不如說取決於無數個在地的選擇——關於街道、公園和住宅，究竟是為誰而建。

discuss: What is one thing you like and one thing you would change about the city or town where you live?
Why do you think so many people move from the countryside to cities?
If you were the mayor for a day, what would you do to make your city more liveable?
